title: Config: add tuning knobs for TP collective timeouts + watchdog sensitivity (deployment-mode defaults)
author: Samir Qureshi
release_notes: Adds new runtime configuration knobs for TP collective timeouts and watchdog sensitivity with documented defaults by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). No behavior change unless overridden.
description: Problem: We currently have hard-coded / loosely-defined thresholds for (a) collective timeouts / async error polling and (b) TP-group forward-progress watchdog sensitivity. In incident and customer escalation contexts, the only mitigation has been broad traffic shifting or disabling TP features, because operators can’t safely tune thresholds without rebuilding or using undocumented env vars. This PR introduces explicit, documented, validated configuration knobs for TP collective timeout thresholds and watchdog sensitivity, including deployment-mode guidance (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). The goal is to enable safer mitigation during rollouts (ENG-2406/ENG-2407) and to make thresholds visible + auditable for SRE/oncall and customer support guidance. Changes: 1) Introduce new config keys (YAML + env override support): - tp.collectives.timeout_ms (env: RW_TP_COLLECTIVES_TIMEOUT_MS) - tp.collectives.async_error_poll_interval_ms (env: RW_TP_ASYNC_ERROR_POLL_INTERVAL_MS) - tp.watchdog.progress_timeout_ms (env: RW_TP_WATCHDOG_PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_MS) - tp.watchdog.sensitivity (enum: conservative|balanced|aggressive; env: RW_TP_WATCHDOG_SENSITIVITY) - tp.watchdog.min_tokens_per_rank_per_sec (env: RW_TP_WATCHDOG_MIN_TOKENS_PER_RANK_PER_SEC) 2) Add validation + clamping: - timeout_ms: [1000, 120000] - poll_interval_ms: [50, 2000] and must be <= timeout_ms/2 - progress_timeout_ms: [2000, 300000] - min_tokens_per_rank_per_sec: [0, 1e6] (0 disables rate-based component) Invalid values fail-fast at startup with a clear error and include the effective config block in logs. 3) Document recommended defaults by deployment mode: - Hosted: balanced watchdog; shorter collective timeout to reduce pooled capacity contamination; enable poll interval 250ms - Dedicated: balanced by default, but recommend conservative for bursty long-streaming workloads; longer progress_timeout - Private: conservative recommended; explicitly call out that some interconnects (esp. older IB configs) may need longer timeout_ms 4) Add startup log line emitting the resolved TP config (sanitized) to make incident triage easier. Notes: - Default behavior is unchanged for release/1.19 unless a new key is set. If no config is present, we continue to use the existing internal defaults. - This PR does not change any watchdog triggering logic; only makes the parameters explicit and validated. (Logic changes are in PR-18462 and PR-18455.) - Support guidance: the keys align with the workarounds we’ve been giving in SUP-9841; we now have a canonical doc location. Checklist: - [x] Backwards compatible config parsing - [x] Unit tests for parsing/validation - [x] Docs updated with examples for Hosted/Dedicated/Private - [x] Release/patch safe (no default changes) Rollout: This will ship in runtime 1.19.x. Dedicated can opt-in via cluster config; Hosted will leave defaults until the canary shows watchdog false positive rates are acceptable. Related: ENG-2406 (collective timeout/error propagation), ENG-2407 (watchdog/quarantine), INT-611 (alerts + runbook clarity).
commits: runtime/config: add TPCollectivesConfig + TPWatchdogConfig structs and validators
runtime/config: parse new tp.collectives.* and tp.watchdog.* keys (yaml + env overrides)
runtime/logging: emit resolved TP config at startup (info, one-time)
docs: add TP timeouts/watchdog tuning section with deployment-mode defaults
tests: add config parsing/validation coverage (invalid ranges, poll interval constraints)
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova: Can we guarantee these new keys don’t inadvertently change defaults when present-but-empty in YAML (e.g., tp: {} in a merged config)? I want to avoid accidental behavior change in Hosted.

Samir Qureshi (author): Good call. Right now we only apply overrides when the leaf keys exist. An empty tp: {} won’t touch anything. I added a test case for merged configs with tp present but without collectives/watchdog leaves.
Hiro Tanaka: For collectives timeout, should we also expose per-collective vs global? I’m worried a single timeout_ms is too coarse for allreduce vs allgather sizes.

Samir Qureshi (author): Agree long term; keeping it global for 1.19 patch scope. The doc explicitly says it’s a global threshold and points to ENG-2406 follow-up for per-op histograms + potentially per-op knobs once we have better distributions.

Rafael Mendes: Please add deployment-mode guidance for Dedicated. We’ve seen customers with long streams + bursty cancellations; I want a documented conservative profile and a clear warning about false positives when min_tokens_per_rank_per_sec is set too high.

Samir Qureshi (author): Added a "Dedicated" subsection with two example profiles (balanced vs conservative) and highlighted that rate-based watchdog should start at 0 (disabled) unless you’ve validated token rate metrics for the model/workload.
Omar El-Sayed: Can we emit the effective config as structured fields (key=value) not just a blob, so it’s searchable in logs?

Samir Qureshi (author): Updated to log as a single JSON-ish structured line with explicit fields: tp_collectives_timeout_ms, tp_async_error_poll_interval_ms, tp_watchdog_progress_timeout_ms, tp_watchdog_sensitivity, tp_watchdog_min_tokens_per_rank_per_sec. Also ensured we don’t dump entire config.
Connor O'Brien: Since this targets release/1.19, please confirm no new mandatory flags. Also add to runtime-1.19 changelog under "Reliability" and link to the doc page.
Samir Qureshi (author): Confirmed optional-only. Added changelog entry + doc link.
Sofia Ivanova: Approving after last push. Thanks for adding the poll_interval constraint; prevents some pathological settings.
Rafael Mendes: Approved. This will help oncall; please follow up with Tomáš/Kira to ensure the runbook references these exact key names.
